records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy intermetallics (HEIs) be used as catalysts for various reactions, including propylene production, acetylene semihydrogenation, hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen reduction reaction, and alcohol oxidation?. System: High-entropy intermetallics (HEIs) with various compositions, such as (PtCoCu)(GeGaSn), (PtCoNi)(SnInGa), (NiFeCu)(GaGe), and (FeCoNi)3(TiAl). Test conditions: Various reactions, including propylene production, acetylene semihydrogenation, hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen reduction reaction, and alcohol oxidation, under different conditions, such as temperature, pressure, and electrolyte. Findings: HEIs exhibit high catalytic activity and stability for various reactions; HEIs can be designed to have specific properties, such as site isolation and electronic structure, to enhance catalytic performance; HEIs show improved durability and resistance to degradation compared to traditional catalysts; HEIs can be used for various reactions, including propylene production, acetylene semihydrogenation, hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen reduction reaction, and alcohol oxidation; HEIs exhibit high mass activity and low overpotential for hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen reduction reaction. Mechanism: The authors propose that the high catalytic activity of HEIs is due to the site isolation effect, electronic structure, and synergistic contribution of multiple elements. Limitations: The authors mention that the synthesis of HEIs can be challenging and that further understanding of the structural and compositional changes of HEIs at the atomic level is necessary. Future work: The authors suggest that establishing an easy, simple, and cost-effective procedure for the synthesis of HEI catalysts with high homogeneity and size control is highly desired. Quote: "the emergence of HEIs demonstrates that we are moving toward the cherished goal in alloy catalysis"
